questions.problem:
For the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{v}^{2}+uv \\ v-u\end{aligned}]
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the point where $[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)={v}^{2}+uv$ and $y(u,v)=v-u.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =v & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =2v+u \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}v & 2v+u \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =v\cdot 1-(2v+u)\cdot (-1) \\  & =v+2v+u \\  & =3v+u.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ the value of our Jacobian determinant is

$$
{\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(8,-2)}=3(-2)+8=2.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Local Area Scale Factor of a Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(1,5)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(uv) \\ u{v}^{2}\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))≈|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\cdot {{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{⏟}}_{\delta A}
$$

 

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{u} & \frac{1}{v} \\ {v}^{2} & 2uv\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\cdot 2uv-\frac{1}{v}\cdot {v}^{2} \\  & =2v-v \\  & =v \\ {\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(1,5)} & =v\,{|}_{u=1\,v=5} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & ≈|5|\cdot \delta A \\  & =5\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Regions Where a Transformation is Orientation-Preserving or Reversing
questions.problem:
Which of the following shows the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{e}^{u+v} \\ -uv\end{aligned}],
$$

is (locally) orientation-preserving?
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that a transformation is (locally) orientation-preserving at the points where the Jacobian determinant is positive:

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}>0.
$$

We have

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{e}^{u+v} \\ -uv\end{aligned}].
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}{e}^{u+v} & {e}^{u+v} \\ -v & -u\end{aligned}| \\  & ={e}^{u+v}\cdot (-u)-(-v)\cdot {e}^{u+v} \\  & ={e}^{u+v}(v-u).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the required regions, we solve the following inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{u+v}(v-u) & >0 \\ v-u & >0 \\ v & >u\end{aligned}
$$

 

Notice that the equation 

$$
v=u
$$

defines a straight line, and the coordinates of, say, $(2,3)$ satisfy the inequality. 

Therefore, the region where the transformation is (locally) orientation-preserving must be the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14052618/assets/8bec16b8ed5083071e21761e6b2e649e136ce0662f7e5ab764161491094c0609.png)

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Regions Where a Transformation is Orientation-Preserving or Reversing
questions.problem:
Which of the following shows the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $T,$ given by 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} \\ u-\frac{1}{3}v\end{aligned}],
$$

is (locally) orientation-reversing?
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that a transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing at the points where the Jacobian determinant is negative:

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}<0
$$

We have

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} \\ u-\frac{1}{3}v\end{aligned}].
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3{u}^{2} & -v \\ 1 & -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}| \\  & =(3{u}^{2})\cdot (-\frac{1}{3})-(1)\cdot (-v) \\  & =v-{u}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the required regions, we solve the following inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}v-{u}^{2} & <0 \\ v & <{u}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Notice that the equation 

$$
v={u}^{2}
$$

defines a parabola, and the coordinates of, say, $(1,-1)$ satisfy the inequality. 

Therefore, the region where the transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing must be the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14052618/assets/1368ee41963c1abcc320d2cd35449c08599582f37c7d68f750e137fcdcd2e57b.png)

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Local Area Scale Factor of a Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(0,3)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡u-{v}^{2} \\ u+v\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))≈|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\cdot {{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{⏟}}_{\delta A}
$$

 

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡u & -2v \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡u)\cdot 1-1\cdot (-2v) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡u+2v \\ {\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(0,3)} & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡u+2v)\,{|}_{u=0\,v=3} \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡0+2(3) \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & ≈|6|\cdot \delta A \\  & =6\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$
